thread:
Maria: Quick heads up — we saw a perf regression on A100-80GB when seq_len > 2048. The kernel selector is choosing the generic matmul path instead of the tensor-core bf16 path. Anyone bumped into this?

Nate: :eyes: saw similar on one infra node last night. nvprof traces looked like a fallback to cublas_gemm. Could be our capability detection returning wrong SM or missing BF16/TC flags.

Leo: Is this only for long sequences or all batches?

Maria: Appears sequence-length dependent. <=2048 uses optimized path (fast), >2048 goes slow. Also interesting: KV cache alignment increases effective seq_len by padding, so some requests cross the threshold.

Ashley: Do we have the raw probe output? I remember a MIG instance once reported compute capability differently.

Maria: Paste from node that regressed:
```
# gpu_probe output
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB
SMs: 108 (compute_capability=8.0)
TensorCores: true
BF16_support: true
FP8_support: false
driver_version: 535.54
cuBLASLt: 2.14.3
```
But our autotuner logged: `selected_kernel=gemm_generic` for shapes (bs=1, seq=3072, hidden=12288).

Harper: Could be our kernel selector heuristics: we currently prefer TC path only when seq_len <= 2048 or when kv_cache_enabled==false. That was added to avoid large shared memory spills, but with BF16 TC we should revisit.

Nate: Another wrinkle: on MIG slices NVML reports reduced SM count and we run a check `if sm_count < 80 then disable_tc`. That heuristic was copy-pasted and might be too aggressive.

Leo: We should add an explicit compute capability check (major >= 8) + feature query for bf16/warp-mma support instead of sm_count threshold. E.g. query cuDeviceGetAttribute(CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_MAJOR, dev).

Ashley: Agree. Also we need to surface why autotuner didn't override the heuristic. Autotuner is supposed to run on first N requests and record microbenchmarks. Was it skipped?

perf-bot: perf run 1769994310: baseline 210 tok/s on tc-bf16 path (seq=2048), observed 87 tok/s on gemm_generic path (seq=3072). Delta -58%.

Maria: I repro'd locally in a simple harness. Adding KV padding of 128 pushes seq to 3072 and selector flips. Suggested quick fix: change selector to prefer TC when bf16_support==true AND hidden%warp_alignment==0, and let autotuner still benchmark in background.

Harper: Can we also add a small profiler check during startup: run a micro-gemm test for two shapes (seq=1536, seq=3072) and pick winner, caching to /var/lib/redwood/gpu_profile.json? That avoids long cold regressions.

Nate: Good idea. Keep it fast (100ms runs) and run only if driver/cuBLAS versions are known-good. Fallback to heuristic if profiling fails.

Ashley: We should also cover FP8 paths — we have code gating fp8 by runtime flag `allow_fp8`. If device reports fp8 but user disallowed, selector must not pick fp8 kernels. Add explicit checks in kernel_selector: device_supports_fp8 && config.allow_fp8.

Leo: For tests: add a CI unit that mocks NVML returning SM=56 (MIG) and compute_cap=8, bf16=true; ensure selector prefers tc for small-large mixes. Mocking NVML is easier than full GPU CI.

ci-bot: Created ticket INF-2312 for the probe + autotune changes and CI mocks. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2312

Maria: Action items: 1) Nate: replace sm_count threshold with explicit compute_cap + feature flags + testcase (INF-2312). 2) Harper: prototype quick micro-gemm profiler and cache. 3) Ashley: add fp8 gating and KV-padding awareness in selector. 4) Leo: add CI NVML mock + unit.

Nate: I'll open a PR with change + a small perf report. Will include the failing trace and the microbench numbers.

Maria: Thanks — would like the PR by EOD tomorrow if possible. This one affects Dedicated customers with large context workloads.

Harper: Also noted: telemetry event `gpu_kernel_choice` should include fields: device_compute_cap, tensor_core_used, reason (heuristic|autotune|profile). I'll add schema change request.

perf-bot: noted. Will emit examples when PR merges.

Maria: Cool. If anyone sees other nodes with mismatched probe outputs drop them here. Reassigning to INF-2312 owners. :thumbsup:
